svg.title: One cell precesses; a population forms a sequence
svg.desc: Three-panel schematic. A: one place cell (Cell 3, teal) crosses its place field on a linear track over five theta cycles; its single spike per cycle falls at 300, 240, 180, 120 and 60 degrees, so it fires progressively earlier in each cycle, and a position-versus-phase plot of the same five spikes descends. The middle cycle is shaded. B: that cycle expanded for five cells whose place fields overlap the animal's current position; Cells 1 to 5 fire at 60, 120, 180, 240 and 300 degrees, so cells with fields behind the animal fire first and cells with fields ahead fire last, all within one theta cycle. C: a CA1 pyramidal neuron receives CA3 input through Schaffer collaterals on proximal apical dendrites and entorhinal layer III input on the distal tuft; light inhibits only the entorhinal terminals in CA1. In mice on a familiar linear track (Guardamagna et al., 2025), this reduced phase-precession slope magnitude and phase range, strengthened population sequence organization, and largely preserved spatial firing. Timing and circuit are schematic.

g.text: A: One cell across successive cycles
Shaded cycle 3 is expanded in B
Schematic: constant running speed; one representative spike per cycle.
Crest = 0°, next crest = 360°. Phase origin arbitrary; consistent throughout.
B: Several cells within one cycle
Within-cycle order is a population measurement.
C: The two measures can change differently
Mice on a familiar linear track
Qualitative summary of reported effects; no values plotted.
